rationale: Up to a winsorization and an industry-linear z-score, this is the exact sign-flipped re-run of the archived UnstableEarningsDebtRaise (same 70th-percentile cash-flow-volatility gate, payload NEG of dltis−dltr), so it will mechanically reproduce that signal's statistics with reversed sign rather than test anything new.

Swapping a hard 70th-percentile gate for a continuous [0,1] volatility rank weight on the same net-repayment payload is a cosmetic parameterization variant of Signal 1 (itself a duplicate of the archived UnstableEarningsDebtRaise), and the smooth weight only shrinks low-volatility firms toward zero rather than changing the underlying economic claim.

Deflating repayment by the existing debt stock is a genuinely different economic construct (retirement capacity vs. financing scale) and usefully decomposes the archive's gross-churn result, though dltr and dltis are highly correlated so this may substantially recover DebtTurnoverUnstableCash, and the small-debt denominator will create an inverse-leverage tilt and unstable extremes that should be checked.

The conditioner-fixed instrument swap is a legitimate discriminating test, but because dividend payment and cash-flow volatility are strongly negatively correlated the high-volatility/high-payout leg will be thin and the signal risks collapsing into a payout-yield main effect weighted by a near-constant rank, so a payer-only or within-payer version would be a cleaner design.

The verification logic (cash distributions cannot be funded by accruals) is coherent and the gate is well-motivated, but it sits close to the published dividends-and-earnings-quality result (Skinner–Soltes) and within the gated subsample the payload is simply payout yield, so the test only adds value if the effect is demonstrably absent or weaker in the cash-backed complement.

The hypothesis claims a "structurally shrinking revenue base" but the expression trends revt/at, i.e. asset turnover, which falls just as readily from asset growth with flat revenue — so the conditioner is a known-anomaly-adjacent turnover/asset-growth composite rather than the top-line decline the economic story requires.
